verdict.rationale: Babylon.js is fundamentally a 3D engine; evidence shows a scene graph that includes sprites and layers, and physics engine integrations (Havok, Cannon.js, Ammo.js, Oimo.js), but these are general 3D physics engines, not dedicated 2D physics, and there is no dedicated tilemap system or 2D-first rendering pipeline mentioned. Community commentary criticizes the physics implementation's rigor but doesn't address 2D-specific workflows at all. missing for 10: dedicated tilemap/2D level-editing tools, 2D-specific physics engine (e.g. box2d-style), documentation or community evidence of 2D being a first-class (not bolted-on) workflow, independent corroboration of sprite/2D workflows in practice.
